newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ budget blowout seen if spendup occurs - NBR poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ budget blowout seen if spendup occurs - NBR poll.

text.p: Most New Zealand business leaders believe there will be a budget blow-out if the coalition government goes through with its forecast spending, the National Business Review weekly reported on Friday.
It said the scepticism was revealed in the second quarterly NBR/Ernst and Young CEO Survey.
Almost 75 percent of the business leaders surveyed thought it unlikely the coalition could fulfil its policy commitments and maintain a government surplus at the same time.
In a speech on Friday setting the scene for Tuesday's budget policy statement (BPS), New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters stressed the need for national savings and tight fiscal management.

"The government, in taking a prudent and conservative approach to fiscal management, is doing its bit by maintaining fiscal surpluses to boost national savings," Peters told a lunchtime meeting of the American Chamber of Commerce in Auckland.
"Responsible and prudent management will be the hallmark of this government's approach to fiscal management."
Peters said spending would be well managed, taxes would be reduced over time and debt would continue to be repaid.
Net public debt is forecast to fall to about 27 percent of GDP this year and to 18.7 percent in 1999/2000.

Tuesday's BPS will tie the coalition agreement between Peters' New Zealand First Party and the conservative National Party, struck after October's general election, into the budget process. It will set the priorities for the June budget and the government's broad approach to fiscal management over the next three years.
The NBR said it would publish in next Friday's issue a full report and analysis of its CEO Survey, which covers intentions of capital investment, the economy and information technology.
